evidence.result: The design explicitly rejects project-wide Actor scope as sufficient, binds project/environment/purpose, derives identity from verified proof and keeps service authentication out of owner/admin routes. No concrete scope escalation is authorized by the plan.

Metadata-only control/browser surface, private ingestion and consumption, server-compiled provider paths, non-root scoped controller authority and deny-by-default policies preserve the declared separation. Default unavailable/sealed behavior is explicit and does not erase mounted static application material.

Redemption must validate actual FoundationEngine grant/lease/context before and after provider I/O, including worker, epoch, fence, cancellation and expiry. Mint-time validation alone is explicitly insufficient.

Intent and stable identities precede external writes; CAS and reconciliation prevent blind replay. Rotation requires a qualified consumer transition plus old upstream revocation evidence. KV versioning and arbitrary owner assertions are explicitly insufficient.

Actual non-dev OpenBao ACL/CAS/revocation and seal/cold-recovery testing is required. PostgreSQL transition, off-host recovery and server/network isolation are not implied by the local lab. Six new acceptance criteria carry named future test IDs, and the implementation order is sequential.

implementation_checks: After an upstream old-key revocation with a lost response, old access may already be unusable. Preserve the actual transition/consumer state as uncertain and reconcile; do not interpret AC-17 as permission to route back blindly or promise that old upstream access still works.

Pin the concrete request/response/provider schemas, byte/time/TTL limits, private CLI proof protocol and rotation state machine before their downstream consumers are implemented. This plan review does not certify those unimplemented details.
